knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 2.6.6
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly describes an F distribution in variance comparison?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: F is a ratio construction with separate numerator and denominator degrees of freedom under independence and Normal-sample conditions.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Scaled ratio of independent Normal-sample variances; two degrees of freedom.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Using t for a variance ratio or ignoring independence and population assumptions.

choices.label: An F variable is a ratio of two independent chi-square variables, each divided by its degrees of freedom. It arises from a scaled ratio of independent sample variances from Normal populations and has two degrees of freedom.
An F variable is the difference of two sample means divided by one pooled standard error.
An F distribution has one degrees-of-freedom parameter because numerator and denominator must have equal sample sizes.
Any ratio of sample variances is exactly F distributed even when samples are dependent or populations are non-Normal.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 2.6.6
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Independent Normal samples of sizes n₁ and n₂ have equal population variances. Which statement is correct?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Each sample variance contributes a chi-square component with n_i-1 degrees of freedom, producing the stated F ratio.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Applying a t law to variance ratios or using n rather than n-1 degrees of freedom.

choices.label: F=S₁²/S₂²~F_{n₁-1,n₂-1} under the equal-variance null, with the numerator and denominator degrees of freedom kept in that order.
S₁²/S₂²~t_{n₁+n₂-2} because both t and F use sample variances.
S₁²/S₂²~F_{n₁,n₂} because estimating sample means does not consume degrees of freedom.
S₁²/S₂² is standard Normal under equal variances because its expected value is near one.

worked_example.title: Variance-ratio F from two independent Normal samples
worked_example.problem_statement: Two independent random samples are drawn from Normal populations with equal variances. Sample 1 has n₁ = 10 and S₁² = 20; sample 2 has n₂ = 8 and S₂² = 10. Form the variance-ratio statistic F = S₁² / S₂², state its null distribution (degrees of freedom), and explain why a one-sample t-statistic is the wrong tool for this comparison.

given.note: second Normal sample, independent of the first

worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Form the ratio of sample variances and attach F(df₁, df₂) with df = n − 1 for each sample.

steps.label: Form the variance ratio
steps.explanation: For independent Normal samples, the ratio of unbiased sample variances is the natural comparison of scale under equal-variance nulls.

steps.label: State the null F distribution
steps.attempt_cue: Name degrees of freedom for numerator and denominator.
steps.explanation: Under σ₁² = σ₂², F ~ F(n₁ − 1, n₂ − 1) = F(9, 7).

steps.label: Refuse using t for that job
steps.attempt_cue: State why a t pivot for a mean is the wrong tool here.
steps.explanation: The t-statistic studentises a mean using one sample's S. Comparing two variances uses the F ratio of sample variances. Substituting a t critical value or a one-sample mean pivot does not answer the variance-ratio question.
steps.calculation: t studentises a mean; F compares two sample variances

worked_example.final_answer: F = 2 ~ F(9, 7) under equal variances. A t-statistic for a mean is the wrong tool for a two-sample variance comparison.
worked_example.common_pitfall: Using t with pooled sd to compare variances, or assigning F degrees of freedom as n₁ and n₂ instead of n₁ − 1 and n₂ − 1.
